sections.h2: Which Spalding County offices touch a tax bill?
sections.html:
Spalding County divides the work among five bodies. The Tax Commissioner bills, collects and passes the money to each taxing body. The Board of Tax Assessors values property and approves exemptions. A Board of Equalization named by the Grand Jury hears disputes the assessors leave unresolved, while the county commissioners and the school board each pick a millage rate.

The Tax Commissioner's office moved to 411 E. Solomon Street in Griffin, three blocks from the courthouse. Doors open at 8:00 on weekdays and close at 4:30, the phone is (770) 467-4360, and mail goes to PO Box 509, Griffin, GA 30224. Call (770) 467-4240 for the Tax Assessor. County administration works from 119 E. Solomon Street.

sections.h2: What is the November deadline in Spalding County, and what do late payers owe?
sections.html:
Bills for land, buildings and business equipment normally fall due on November 15. The Tax Commissioner says late fees do not start until 60 days after the bills go out. Past the due date, interest builds each month at the legal rate, and a 5% penalty lands every 120 days until the total reaches 20%.

A homesteaded property owing under $500 escapes the penalty. Mobile and modular homes run on another calendar: the tax is due April 1, and the owner needs to file a return and pay in full to receive a location permit, with a 10% penalty if the owner skips both. Unpaid tax lets the Tax Commissioner levy on the property, a step the office calls a last resort.

sections.h2: What are the key Spalding County tax rules at a glance?
sections.html:
Spalding County property tax rules, from the Spalding County Tax Commissioner's website
TopicRule as the county prints it
Assessed value40% of fair market value
Return seasonOpens January 1 and closes April 1
Land and building billsDue November 15
Appeal cutoffForty-five days after the notice mailing date
Homestead filingMust arrive ahead of April 1 to count for the same tax year
Mobile home taxDue April 1
Delinquent tax salesHeld on a first Tuesday, 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

A mill is one thousandth of a dollar per dollar of assessed value. The county's order of operations is to subtract exemptions from the 40% assessed value first and apply the millage rate to what remains.

sections.h2: What is the route for contesting a Spalding County value?
sections.html:
The cutoff is forty-five days after the assessment notice is mailed. The county lists three grounds for an appeal: whether the property is taxable, what it is worth, and whether that worth is uniform with similar properties. A complaint about the size of the tax bill is not a ground.

The Board of Tax Assessors looks at the appeal first and reports its decision. A taxpayer still unhappy can go to the county Board of Equalization or choose arbitration, and a judgment from either can be carried to Superior Court. For tax year 2026, the county Tax Commissioner stretched the homestead filing window to match the appeal period, June 5 through July 23, 2026, and that period has ended. Exemptions based on income had to be requested in person with proof of 2025 income.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions does Spalding County offer?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner lists state and local exemptions combined. The main ones:

  • Standard homestead: $2,000 each from the state, county and school portions, with no income test.
  • Standard elderly: age 65 before January 1, net income capped at $15,000, with bigger county and school deductions.
  • School exemption: age 62 or older, or totally disabled at any age, with household gross income capped at $12,500.
  • Ages 65 to 69, $10,000 off the school portion regardless of income; ages 70 to 74, $20,000; ages 75 and older, $30,000.
  • A floating school exemption for owners 65 and up, which freezes the value used for school tax.

Once granted, an exemption renews each year until the owner moves or qualifies for a different type. A buyer must apply for the new address. A separate deferral program serves owners 62 and older whose gross household income stays under $15,000; the deferral can run until the property changes hands or the deferred tax plus interest reaches 85% of fair market value. Ask the Tax Commissioner whether a deferral applies to your house before you list it.

sections.h2: What does the Census show for Spalding County sellers?
sections.html:
Census figures for Spalding County show 70,775 people in mid-2025, a 5.2% rise from the 2020 base, living among 29,850 housing units. The middle home value is $228,700 and owners occupy 62.7% of housing units. Monthly rent in the middle of the range is $1,113, and households in the middle earn $62,071 a year. About one in five residents (20.6%) is past 65, so the senior exemptions above apply to many sellers.

The county covers 195.97 square miles of land with 343.5 people per square mile, and Griffin is where the courthouse, tax office and clerk all sit. The county's own news page notes a comprehensive plan update that looks toward 2050 and the county commissioners' adoption of a full rollback rate for 2025, which can come up in buyer conversations.

sections.h2: How are delinquent taxes and tax sales handled in Spalding County?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner's FAQ explains that Georgia law puts delinquent tax sales on a month's first Tuesday, within a 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. window. The sale takes place at 411 E. Solomon Street. Bidders register on sale morning between 8:00 and 9:30, must be at least 18, and show a driver's license or other official ID. Bidding usually starts around 10:00 or 10:30.

Notices run in the Griffin Daily News on Tuesdays starting four weeks before a sale, and the office posts the sale list on its site. Excess funds requests for tax sale proceeds need original documents, and the office accepts no email. If a house you own faces a sale, contact the Tax Commissioner before the advertising starts.

sections.h2: Where do I record the deed or get a copy in Spalding County?
sections.html:
The Clerk of Superior Court keeps deeds, at 132 E. Solomon Street in Griffin. Office hours run from 8:00 in the morning to 5:00 in the afternoon on weekdays, the main number is 770-467-4309, and one deputy clerk is assigned to real estate. The Tax Commissioner's FAQ sends owners to this office for a copy of a warranty deed.

Spalding County's Community Development department at 119 E. Solomon Street covers planning, zoning and permits for unincorporated Spalding County. Its Planning Commission meets the last Tuesday of the month at 6:00 p.m., and its Board of Appeals meets the second Thursday of the month at 6:00 p.m. Call the department before you start repair work if the house sits outside the city of Griffin. Its contact list also names a business and alcohol license technician and a permit technician, so ask for the right desk when you call.

faqs.q: What is the Spalding County payment deadline?
faqs.a: November 15 for real estate and business personal property. Late fees wait until 60 days after the bills are mailed, and mobile and modular homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: What is the appeal cutoff after a Spalding County assessment notice?
faqs.a: Forty-five days after the notice is mailed. The appeal starts with the Board of Tax Assessors and can continue to the Board of Equalization or arbitration, and then to Superior Court.

faqs.q: What is the Spalding County late penalty?
faqs.a: Interest runs monthly at the legal rate after the due date, plus a 5% penalty every 120 days until it totals 20%. A homesteaded property with tax under $500 is excused from the penalty.

faqs.q: Where is the Spalding County Tax Commissioner's office?
faqs.a: 411 E. Solomon Street in Griffin, GA 30223, phone (770) 467-4360. It opens at 8:00 on weekdays and closes at 4:30, and mail goes to PO Box 509, Griffin, GA 30224.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Spalding County house that owes back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, though the Tax Commissioner can levy on unpaid property and sell it at a tax sale. Request a payoff figure that includes interest and penalties so the balance can be settled from your closing proceeds.
